clue.text: One aboard Dutch fishing vessel to plague European neighbour?

parts.note: to dog someone is to plague or pester them
Germany borders the Netherlands, so a German is a European neighbour of the Dutch

explanation.surface: A Dutch fisherman is accused of tormenting the people next door.
explanation.walkthrough: A dogger is a two-masted Dutch fishing boat, so the definition is the whole opening phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A doggerman is a sailor who crews a dogger, the traditional Dutch fishing boat.

clue.text: Size of slate, Dutch, used to cover part of pontoon deck

indicators.note: in a down entry, something that covers another sits on top of it, so the first piece comes above the second

parts.note: Du. is the dictionary abbreviation for Dutch
a chess is one of the planks forming the deck of a pontoon bridge

explanation.surface: A Dutch slate is laid over part of a floating bridge's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: Pontoon suggests the card game; here it is a floating bridge, whose deck planks are called chesses.
explanation.definitionFit: In roofing, a duchess is a standard slate size, 24 by 12 inches, among a series named after noble ranks.

clue.text: Old Semitic tongue, one lost at start of century before OT book?

indicators.note: something lost at the start is dropped from the front of the word that follows

parts.note: one is the article a
an age is a long period such as a century
Ez. is the abbreviation for Ezra, a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A scholar dates an ancient language by its losses and its place before a biblical book.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the A from AGE, then add the abbreviation for Ezra.
explanation.definitionFit: Ge'ez is the ancient Semitic language of Ethiopia, still used in its church liturgy.

clue.text: Wild daisy, green and pale

parts.note: a green traffic light means go
wan means pale and sickly

explanation.surface: A daisy in the wild is described as green and pallid.
explanation.definitionFit: Gowan is the Scots and northern name for the daisy, especially the wild one.

clue.text: A miscellany of lieder collected in the past

indicators.note: a miscellany is a jumbled collection, so the word that follows is mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone once gathered a varied collection of German songs.
explanation.walkthrough: Lieder are German art songs; 'in the past' flags an obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: Relide is a Spenserian past tense of an old verb meaning to gather or assemble.

clue.text: Mosque menial allowing Jesuits in

indicators.note: allowing someone in means letting them inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a maid is a menial servant
SJ stands for Society of Jesus, the Jesuit order

explanation.surface: A mosque's servant lets members of a Catholic order inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Masjid is the Arabic word for a mosque, a Muslim place of worship.

clue.text: Protective temple ornaments — insurance company protects ten if damaged

indicators.note: damaged things are knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
something that protects surrounds and shields what it guards

parts.note: AXA is a large international insurance company
these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An insurer covers damage to ornaments on a temple.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled TEN IF goes after the first A of AXA.
explanation.definitionFit: Antefixa are the upright ornamental tiles along the eaves of classical temples, covering the ends of the roof tiles.

clue.text: E.g. stirrups, see, on Arab that's uncontrolled without one

indicators.note: an uncontrolled horse runs wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder
without one means a single letter standing for one is removed

parts.note: taken as written
one is the article a

explanation.surface: Riding stirrups are noticed on a runaway Arab horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Stirrups look like riding tack; the stirrup is also a small bone of the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: The stirrup, or stapes, is one of the three ossicles of the middle ear, so it is an example.

clue.text: US party boss to knock flat with editorial (11, two words)

parts.note: to floor someone is to knock them down
a newspaper's leader is its editorial

explanation.surface: An American politician is flattened by a scathing newspaper opinion piece.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US Congress, a floor leader is the party member who directs the party's business in the chamber.

clue.text: Earthenware duck inside shell

indicators.note: inside places the first piece within the second

parts.note: a clam is a shellfish, here standing for its shell
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A pottery duck has something hidden inside its shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloam is a dialect word, chiefly from Cornwall and Devon, for earthenware pottery.

clue.text: Progress with arms support to China I organized

indicators.note: organized means put into a new order, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Military support is sent to China to make progress in an arms race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arms' suggests weapons, but it means the limbs that swing an ape through the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Brachiation is the way gibbons and other apes move, swinging hand over hand from branch to branch.

clue.text: Ale old Nan brewed for the whole group (9, three words)

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients together, so the words before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Grandma has made beer for the entire family.
explanation.definitionFit: One and all means everybody without exception, the whole company together.

clue.text: Tapestry yarn wife kept in basket or old pot — little left

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a creel is a wicker basket, as used by anglers
W is the abbreviation for wife
a second, independent route: CREWE is an obsolete word for a pot, and L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: An embroiderer's wool is stored in a basket or an old pot with little remaining.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue offers a second route: CREWE, an old word for a pot, plus L for left. Either wordplay alone gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Crewel is a fine worsted wool used for embroidery and tapestry work.

clue.text: West African castle, back to front

indicators.note: the back letter is moved round to the front of the word

parts.note: the castle in chess is also called a rook

explanation.surface: A fort on the West African coast is described as reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back to front' here does not reverse the word; only its last letter moves to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kroo are a people of the Liberian coast, famed as seamen, and a Kroo is a member of that people.

clue.text: Synagogue 'performer' hard on muezzin's effort?

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
the azan is the call to prayer chanted by the muezzin

explanation.surface: A synagogue singer is judged severely against the mosque's call to prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazan, or cantor, leads the singing of prayers in a synagogue, hence a performer of sorts.

clue.text: 'Desert Rat', awful bore? Rommel's certainly admitting it

indicators.note: awful means very bad, so the word beside it is reshaped into a different order
admitting means letting something in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Rommel was a German general, and ja is German for yes, certainly
these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A veteran of the North Africa campaign is found tedious even by his German opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: The Desert Rats were the British 7th Armoured Division fighting Rommel in North Africa; their emblem was this rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: The jerboa is a jumping desert rodent, literally a desert rat, hence the quotation marks.

clue.text: Women in scarlet stuff take in unfashionable bar

indicators.note: in places the first piece within the word that follows

parts.note: lac is a red resinous substance used in dyes
W is the abbreviation for women

indicators.note: to take something in is to enclose it within something else

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
R stands for recipe, Latin for take, as on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Women wearing bright red outfits are taken into an old-fashioned bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' is R because prescriptions begin with R, short for Latin recipe. 'Bar' is not a pub but the court.
explanation.definitionFit: The bar is the court of law, where barristers plead and prisoners stand for trial.

clue.text: Deviant rites among artful kind

indicators.note: deviant means departing from the norm, so the word after it is rearranged
among puts the first piece in the midst of the second

parts.note: sly means artful and cunning
these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Strange ceremonies are practised among a cunning sort of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' looks like a noun meaning sort, but it is the adjective meaning caring.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisterly means affectionate and caring, as a good sister would be towards a sibling.

clue.text: Duke provided class, unlike of old

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
if means provided that
a form is a class in a British school

explanation.surface: A duke supplied a class of people quite different from in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Difform is an obsolete adjective meaning irregular in shape, or dissimilar.

clue.text: Jock's trick has confounded earlier bid

indicators.note: confounded means thrown into confusion, so the word before it is jumbled

parts.note: these letters are rearranged
to vie is to bid or compete; earlier places this piece after the shuffled one in reading order

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's ploy has spoiled the opening bid at cards.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is a nickname for a Scot, so the definition asks for a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Shavie is a Scots word for a trick or prank.

clue.text: Scottish reel: it is not permitted with English, thrill for Scots

parts.note: in Scots a reel can mean a loud noise or uproar
NL stands for non licet, Latin for it is not permitted
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A Highland dance is banned alongside English customs, which thrills the Scots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scottish reel' looks like the dance, but in Scots reel can also mean a clatter or din.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinnle is a Scots word meaning to tingle or vibrate, or a thrill.

clue.text: Tide rising it leaves dingy at sea going round and round

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read from bottom to top, backwards
at sea means confused, so the word before it is jumbled
when something leaves, it departs and is removed

parts.note: read backwards
taken as written, and removed
these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: As the tide comes in, it leaves a scruffy little boat adrift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dingy' is a plain adjective here, not a misspelt dinghy, though the surface wants a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddying describes water or air swirling in circles, as in a whirlpool.

clue.text: To camp out in US, I occupied a position with silence all round

indicators.note: something all round another encloses it on every side

parts.note: sh is a call for silence
I was means I occupied a position, as in I was there

explanation.surface: A camper in America sat quietly with silence all around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All round' finishes the container instruction begun by 'with'.
explanation.definitionFit: Siwash is a US slang verb meaning to camp out with minimal gear, from a word for a Native American.

clue.text: To walk swayingly after the Scotch, ex-footballer, male imbibes rum litre

definitions.text: To walk swayingly after the Scotch

indicators.note: to imbibe is to drink in, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: he is a male person
rum means odd
L is the abbreviation for litre

explanation.surface: A former footballer staggers home after drinking Scotch, rum and plenty more.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions plus wordplay. Glenn Hoddle played for and managed England. 'After the Scotch' means in Scots usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoddle is Scots for to waddle, and Glenn Hoddle is a well-known former England footballer.

clue.text: Top CD with former lover to the fore?

indicators.note: to the fore means placed at the front, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
the letter C spelt out as CEE, followed by D

explanation.surface: A chart-topping record is credited to someone's former partner.
explanation.walkthrough: CEE is the dictionary spelling of the letter name C.
explanation.definitionFit: To top something is to go beyond it, so the verb means surpass.

clue.text: Political slogan succeeded after revolutionary noise

indicators.note: after puts the first piece behind the second in the answer

parts.note: these letters are rearranged
S is the abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: A rallying cry is chanted after the din of a rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: In family trees, s. stands for succeeded.
explanation.definitionFit: Enosis, union of Cyprus with Greece, was the rallying cry of Greek Cypriot nationalists.

clue.text: Offspring catching a caterpillar in the grass

indicators.note: catching something means holding it inside, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a son is offspring
taken as written
a Caterpillar is a tracked vehicle, short name cat

explanation.surface: A child catches a caterpillar in the long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: The caterpillar is not the larva but the tracked vehicle, a Caterpillar or cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacaton is a coarse grass of the south-western United States, used for hay and pasture.

clue.text: Organs played orally, centre of tongues inserted in bar

indicators.note: inserted in means placed inside the next word

parts.note: sans means without, as bar means except

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter, taken alone

parts.note: the middle letter of the seven

explanation.surface: Church organs are played by mouth, with tongues in the middle of a bar of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organs played orally' are mouth organs, not church instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: A sang is a Chinese mouth organ, a variant of sheng, blown rather than keyed.

clue.text: Sight a —? Strange — can you spot the organism?

definitions.text: Sight a —? Strange — can you spot the organism?

indicators.note: strange means odd and out of order, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the dash is a minus sign, so those words are taken away from what follows

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, and subtracted

explanation.surface: A puzzle challenges you to spot a tiny organism under the microscope.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: remove the letters of SIGHT A from THE ORGANISM and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A moner was Haeckel's name for a simple structureless microscopic organism, which you would struggle to spot.

clue.text: Agreed sound quality in …

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the next one

tone is the quality of a sound

clue.text: … Commercial plugging dwarf creeper

clue.text: Wine from east Italy? North-west actually

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the geographical fib: the wine's town lies in Piedmont, north-west Italy.

clue.text: Pacific coral island undiluted except for odd bits

clue.text: Second-generation immigrant, Carmen — adapts to Americanness

indicators.note: adapts means changes to fit, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the dash works as a minus sign, so the name before it is taken away from the word after

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, and subtracted

clue.text: Typical of thuggish type thrilling girl in love? Not very

clue.text: Lid-lifter casts gaze on Herts community
